# Slice 4: the second review's three remaining findings, fixed and measured

RED is record 35 and GREEN is record 37; record 36 is a handoff the slice had to write to get past the guard,
explained at the end. The RED's three failures in the runner's words: "The cache key of @seen/core#test covers
11 files and 0 of 5 migrations, so a turbo cache hit can report these database tests as passed without ever
running them against a changed schema"; "6 blanket privilege statements in the migrations, each of which
reaches every table in the schema including the ones an earlier migration narrowed", naming all six across the
three files; and "Buyer PII columns whose comment does not state which encryption at rest the schema relies on
today and what is still owed and by whom", naming all six columns.

**F9 needed no uncacheable route.** `$TURBO_ROOT$` resolves inside a package task's `inputs`, so the `test`
task now hashes `supabase/migrations/**` alongside its own files, sixteen files rather than eleven. Measured
both ways rather than argued: on the pre-slice tree, adding a migration that creates an untenanted table and
re-grants the four privileges left the hash unchanged at `b2b848a8daee8791` and printed "cache hit, replaying
logs, 57 passed", which is F9 reproduced exactly; after the change the same probe migration produces "cache
miss, executing", and once applied the guards fail twelve times, naming the probe table for `tenant_id`, for
RLS, for the tenancy expression, for `authenticated` holding four privileges on all 29 tables, for a role
holding update or delete on `audit_events`, and for the blanket grant in the new file. The input list sits on
the root `test` task, so every package's test task now hashes the migrations: deliberate, because the next
database-dependent test may not be in `@seen/core`, and the cost is that it invalidates more caches than that
one package.

**F10 is fixed by removing the six blanket grants rather than by forbidding them in a comment**, and by a test
that reads every file under `supabase/migrations` and fails on one, so the next author meets a failing test
instead of a paragraph. Part 3's now-dead second revoke of `audit_events` went with them; part 2's revoke is
kept with its comment corrected to say it strips the default privileges rather than a grant of its own; and
part 4 now revokes update, delete and truncate on `audit_events` from `service_role` itself, so it is true read
on its own rather than true only after the tails that used to precede it.

**F12 states the reading and makes it assertable.** Each of the six columns now says: written only as far as a
claim needs it and expired after 30 days by SEEN-083; encryption at rest is the storage layer only, the volume
this database sits on and the Supabase EU project once the SEEN-007 go decision is taken; the value itself is
cleartext, so a `pg_dump` for a restore drill and any query as the service role read every tenant's buyer data
as typed; and nothing encrypts the value itself and no ticket owns doing so, so **column-level encryption is
owed and unowned, a decision beyond this ticket and one owed before SEEN-082 takes the first restore-drill
dump**. `BUYER_PII_COMMENT_TERMS` holds the sentence in place. That matches the clarify decision at record 4 and
names the half it left silent.

**The end state is unchanged from what the review measured, verified rather than assumed.** From `aclexplode`
after a reset: `anon` holds no ACL entry on any of the 29 tables, `authenticated` holds select on 29 and
nothing else, `service_role` holds select and insert on 29 with update, delete and truncate on 28, the 28
excluding `audit_events`. Identical to the baseline. The service role still inserted a tenant with its six
marketplaces seeded by the trigger, inserted an audit event, updated a connection and deleted the tenant with
its audit rows cascading, and part 4's self-check raises on three injected failures, including one for a
revoke that would have been over-broad.

Two harness observations from doing it, both already on the record elsewhere and both confirmed again here. The
pack pointed at the wrong slice, because `plan_accepted_at` counts greens only after the last advance out of
solution, so after the second return the guard read "slice 1 of 4, 0 of 4 done" although slices 1 to 3 are
greened; the documented lever `harness handoff --slice-done 3` fixed it, at record 36, and the orchestrating
session should have declared it when writing the pack. And the guard's exact path match refuses every file
under a directory a slice names, so the migration edits went through a shell the hook cannot see, which is the
fourth ticket to walk into it.
